data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose drive type and health

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.Description
data.value: Identifies HDD, SSD or NVMe for each physical drive and reads predictive health status (SMART/NVMe Health), without repairing anything.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Queries MSFT_PhysicalDisk (Storage Management API), which covers SATA S.M.A.R.T. and NVMe Health without an additional driver.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not repair, format, or move data.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.storage-health.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Reports every detected physical drive; Windows may not expose complete health data for every controller or enclosure.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose Windows build and driver versions

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.Description
data.value: Reads the exact Windows build and video, network, audio, chipset, storage, USB, and Bluetooth driver versions when identifiable.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Queries Win32_PnPSignedDriver (WMI), grouped by device class, plus Environment.OSVersion for the build.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not install, update, or roll back any driver.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-versions.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Chipset uses a name heuristic, and the other categories depend on the device classes manufacturers expose to Windows.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose resolution, refresh rate and HAGS

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.Description
data.value: Compares the configured refresh rate with the maximum supported at the current resolution and reads HAGS state.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Uses EnumDisplaySettings (Win32) for the current/maximum mode and the GraphicsDrivers registry for HwSchMode.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change resolution, refresh rate, or HAGS.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.display-configuration.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: G-SYNC/FreeSync/VRR have no public API without the manufacturer's driver; the app reports this instead of guessing.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose Game Mode, fullscreen and power plan

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.Description
data.value: Reads the current state of Game Mode, fullscreen optimizations and the active power plan, without changing anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the same registry values used by the Game Mode and capture actions, plus the active power scheme.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not enable or disable anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.session-settings.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Only reports the current state; use the corresponding profile actions to apply changes.

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose combined throttling signals

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.Description
data.value: Combines clock drop under load, hardware error events (WHEA) and available temperature to flag "possible throttling", without a direct per-core sensor.

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Combines Win32_Processor (clock), a CPU usage sample, recent WHEA events, and the ACPI thermal zone when available.

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change the power plan, affinity, or priority.

data.name: Actions.safety.throttling-signal.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Without a direct per-core sensor, the result is always presented as "possible," never as certain.

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose current CPU, disk, GPU and network usage

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.Description
data.value: Takes an instantaneous (not averaged) reading of CPU, disk, GPU (when available) and network throughput.

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Uses PerformanceCounter for CPU/disk/GPU (the native "GPU Engine" category) and network interface counters for throughput.

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not set process priority or affinity.

data.name: Actions.safety.resource-usage.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is a short sample (~300 ms), not a sustained average; GPU data may not be available on all hardware.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose GPU PCIe link

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.Description
data.value: Attempts to read the current/maximum PCIe link width and speed of each GPU via Windows device properties, no third-party driver.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Uses CM_Get_DevNode_Property (cfgmgr32) with the standard Windows PCIe link DEVPKEYs.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not reconfigure the bus or slot.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.pcie-link.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Not every driver or motherboard exposes these properties; when they are unavailable, the app reports that instead of guessing.

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose BIOS age and hardware stability

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.Description
data.value: Reads the BIOS release date and recent hardware error (WHEA) events from the Windows Event Log.

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Queries Win32_BIOS (WMI) and events from the Microsoft-Windows-WHEA-Logger source in the System log.

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not update the BIOS or clear the event log.

data.name: Actions.safety.hardware-stability.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Resizable BAR/Above 4G/Smart Access Memory cannot be detected reliably without a manufacturer tool; the app reports this limitation instead of guessing.

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.Name
data.value: Classify the likely bottleneck type

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.Description
data.value: Combines CPU/GPU/disk usage, memory, temperature and the top CPU-consuming process to point to the most likely limiting resource right now.

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Combines resource usage, temperature, memory, available VRAM and the process currently using the most CPU (Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfProc_Process).

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not terminate or prioritize any process.

data.name: Actions.safety.bottleneck-classification.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is an elimination-based classification using local signals. It does not infer external causes or treat cumulative network counters as evidence of a current bottleneck.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose GTA V launch parameters

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.Description
data.value: Reads standalone GTA V Legacy's commandline.txt (never FiveM, which ignores this file) and warns when repair parameters were left permanently active.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads commandline.txt from the standalone GTA V installation folder, if it exists.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change the file.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: FiveM ignores GTA's commandline.txt (a documented FiveM restriction); this diagnostic is relevant only to users who also play standalone GTA V.

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.Name
data.value: Recommend graphics preset

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.Description
data.value: Analyzes GPU, VRAM, CPU, RAM and monitor refresh rate to suggest which graphics preset (FPS, Balanced or Quality) fits the hardware best, without applying anything by itself.

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Combines the existing GPU/VRAM, CPU, RAM, and monitor diagnostics into a simple preset recommendation.

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: only provides a recommendation; the user decides which preset to apply manually.

data.name: Actions.safety.graphics-preset-recommendation.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is a heuristic based on local hardware; it does not consider the server being used or the result of a benchmark that has not yet been run.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose configured texture quality vs. available VRAM

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.Description
data.value: Compares the texture quality configured in FiveM/GTA V with the detected GPU VRAM and warns when the configuration likely exceeds available VRAM.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads TextureQuality from the existing graphics file and the VRAM already read by the GPU diagnostic, applying a documented conservative threshold.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change any graphics setting.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.texture-vram-fit.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is a VRAM-threshold estimate, not an actual measurement of memory usage while the game is running.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose FiveM cache size and integrity

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.Description
data.value: Measures the total and per-category size of FiveM Legacy cache (server-cache, server-cache-priv, NUI storage, logs, diagnostics) and flags files locked by another process, without deleting anything.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Walks the known FiveM Legacy cache/data folders, totals each one's size, and tries to open every file with exclusive access to detect whether another process has locked it.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not delete or move any files.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.cache-storage.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Lock detection is an exclusive-open test at the time of the reading; a file may become locked or unlocked seconds later.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose FiveM installation health

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.Description
data.value: Checks for duplicate installations, write permission on the data folder, OneDrive syncing and free disk space, without changing anything.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Compares known installation candidates (the registry and CitizenFX.ini), tests write access to the data folder, compares the path with the OneDrive-synced folder, and reads free space on the installation drive.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not delete, move, or reinstall anything.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.installation-health.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Duplicate installation detection is a known-path heuristic; installations in unconventional locations may not be found.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose recurring crash and streaming error patterns

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.Description
data.value: Looks for recognizable error codes in recent crash dump names and streaming error keywords (textures, models, maps) in the latest log, without deleting anything.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the names of recent dump files for known error codes and searches the latest FiveM log text for streaming-related keywords.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: An informational message always completes the action; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not open, remove, or send any dump.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-patterns.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is a text search for known patterns, not a memory dump analysis; an absent pattern does not guarantee the problem is absent.

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.Name
data.value: Clean old temporary files

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.Description
data.value: Removes old temporary files that are not in use.

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.DetectionSummary
data.value: Scans the user's Temp folder for files older than the retention period.

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that the selected old files no longer exist after cleanup.

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.UndoSummary
data.value: Irreversible: old temporary files are not preserved in quarantine.

data.name: Actions.storage.user-temporary-files.clean.RiskLimitations
data.value: Removes only old files belonging to the current user; it never touches system folders.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.Name
data.value: Remove old diagnostic files

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.Description
data.value: Removes old FiveM Legacy dumps and logs while preserving recent diagnostics.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.DetectionSummary
data.value: Lists FiveM dumps and logs older than the retention period.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that old diagnostic files were removed and recent ones were preserved.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.UndoSummary
data.value: Irreversible: old diagnostic files are not copied to the journal.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.crash-dumps.prune.RiskLimitations
data.value: Dumps can be useful for support; only those outside the retention period are removed.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.Name
data.value: Repair server cache

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.Description
data.value: Removes only regenerable FiveM Legacy server-content caches when a repair is needed.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.DetectionSummary
data.value: Measures the size of server-cache and server-cache-priv under the FiveM installation.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only regenerable caches were removed.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.UndoSummary
data.value: Regenerable data: FiveM downloads the content again the next time a server is accessed.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.server-cache.repair.RiskLimitations
data.value: The first load will be slower; old Rockstar Editor clips may stop working.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.Name
data.value: Terminate a stuck FiveM process

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.Description
data.value: Terminates a demonstrably stuck and unresponsive FiveM process. This may release files still held by that instance, but it is never part of automatic profiles.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.DetectionSummary
data.value: Checks for a process whose executable belongs to the FiveM installation and has Responding=false (it does not respond to interface messages).

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Terminates the process only after confirming that it is not responding; if it responds normally, the action does nothing.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.UndoSummary
data.value: Irreversible: a terminated process cannot be restored to its previous state.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.stuck-process.terminate.RiskLimitations
data.value: Terminates only processes whose executable belongs to the FiveM installation folder; never third-party, GTA V, or system processes. Any unsaved work in that stuck process is lost.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.Name
data.value: Recreate FiveM local data

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.Description
data.value: Removes and recreates regenerable FiveM Legacy data folders (server-cache, server-cache-priv, logs, crashes) while preserving game-storage, NUI storage, ipfs, CitizenFX.ini and plugins, with quarantine backup.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.DetectionSummary
data.value: Confirms that FiveM is closed and lists files in the known regenerable folders (never those protected by docs/safety.md).

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Moves regenerable files to quarantine before confirming; no protected data is touched.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.UndoSummary
data.value: Regenerable data: reversible from quarantine until the optimization is finally confirmed; afterward, FiveM downloads the content again.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.local-data.recreate.RiskLimitations
data.value: This does not reinstall FiveM or download or run an installer; it only recreates data folders already approved for conditional cleanup in docs/safety.md.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.Name
data.value: Repair corrupted entitlement data

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.Description
data.value: Removes ros_id.dat and the digital entitlements folder only when a startup entitlement error pattern is detected in the latest log, with quarantine backup and per-run confirmation.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the latest FiveM log for a known entitlement or authentication error pattern before touching any file.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Removes ros_id.dat and the entitlements folder only when the error pattern was found; otherwise, it does nothing.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.UndoSummary
data.value: Reversible from quarantine until the optimization is finally confirmed; afterward, FiveM requires a new sign-in to regenerate the data.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.auth-data.repair.RiskLimitations
data.value: Exception action documented in docs/safety.md: ros_id.dat and entitlements are normally never removed automatically; this action exists only for the specific detected error scenario, never in automatic profiles, and always with reversible quarantine.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.Name
data.value: Enable Game Mode

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.Description
data.value: Helps Windows prioritize resources while you play.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the AutoGameModeEnabled value from the current user's registry.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that Game Mode is enabled after the write.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the previous registry value is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.game-mode.enable.RiskLimitations
data.value: The benefit depends on the hardware and Windows version; it may have no noticeable effect.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.Name
data.value: Prefer the high-performance GPU

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.Description
data.value: Sets the Windows graphics preference for detected FiveM Legacy launchers and renderers.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the graphics preference registered for the FiveM executable.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that the high-performance preference is registered.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the previous preference is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.high-performance-gpu.prefer.RiskLimitations
data.value: Only makes a difference on computers with more than one GPU.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.Name
data.value: Disable background capture

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.Description
data.value: Prevents automatic background recording without removing Game Bar.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the background recording (Game DVR) value from the current user's registry.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that background capture is disabled.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the previous value is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.background-capture.disable.RiskLimitations
data.value: Does not remove Game Bar or affect recordings that you start manually.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.Name
data.value: Activate a high-performance power plan

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.Description
data.value: Uses a stronger power mode while the PC is plugged in.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the active power plan and checks whether the computer is plugged in.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that the performance power plan is active.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the previous power plan is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.performance-session.enable.RiskLimitations
data.value: Applied only while plugged in; it increases power consumption and temperature while active.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.graphics.light.apply.Name
data.value: Tune light FiveM graphics

data.value: Disables only the most expensive antialiasing in the existing FiveM file, with a backup.

data.value: Changes only options already present; it does not distribute a generic XML file.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.graphics.balanced.apply.Name

data.value: Confirms that the balanced limits were applied and the file remains valid.

data.value: Fully reversible: the file backup is restored during rollback.

data.value: Confirms that demanding options were reduced and the file remains valid.

data.name: Actions.fivem.legacy.graphics.aggressive.apply.UndoSummary

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.Name
data.value: Tune light GTA V graphics

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.Description
data.value: Finds GTA V Legacy settings.xml, reduces only expensive existing options and creates a backup.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the existing options from GTA V Legacy's settings.xml.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only expensive options were adjusted and the file remains valid.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the file backup is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.graphics.light.apply.RiskLimitations

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.Name
data.value: Apply GTA V graphics launch parameters

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.Description
data.value: Writes the official -cityDensity, -anisotropicQualityLevel, -fxaa, -grassQuality, -lodScale and -frameLimit parameters to standalone GTA V's commandline.txt, preserving any other existing line. Never part of automatic profiles.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the existing commandline.txt (or treats it as empty when absent) and identifies which managed lines are already present.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only managed lines were added or updated and all other lines in the file were preserved.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the file backup is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.graphics.apply.RiskLimitations
data.value: Relevant only to standalone GTA V; FiveM ignores this file. Values use documented conservative limits; the exact unit of -frameLimit is not officially confirmed.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.Name
data.value: Apply GTA V display launch parameters

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.Description
data.value: Writes the display mode (-fullscreen/-windowed/-borderless) and, when chosen, the DirectX version (-DX10/-DX10_1/-DX11) to standalone GTA V's commandline.txt. Never changes resolution. Never part of automatic profiles.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the existing commandline.txt (or treats it as empty when absent) and identifies the configured display and DirectX modes.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only the display-mode and DirectX lines were added or updated and all other lines in the file were preserved.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the file backup is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.display.apply.RiskLimitations
data.value: Does not change -width/-height, resolution, or refresh rate; those changes would require validating the combination against the monitor's supported modes, which the product does not yet do end to end.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.Name
data.value: Apply GTA V repair launch parameters

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.Description
data.value: Writes temporary repair parameters (-safemode, -useMinimumSettings, -UseAutoSettings) to standalone GTA V's commandline.txt to diagnose a specific problem. Never part of automatic profiles and should not stay active permanently.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the existing commandline.txt (or treats it as empty when absent) and identifies which repair parameters are already present.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only the selected repair parameters were added and all other lines in the file were preserved.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: use "Revert this optimization" as soon as you finish diagnosing so the repair parameter is not left active permanently.

data.name: Actions.gtav.legacy.launch-parameters.repair.apply.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is a repair parameter, not a daily optimization; leaving it active indefinitely may reduce graphics quality unnecessarily.

data.value: Reads the video adapters from the registry and the GPU preference already configured for FiveM.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gpu-preference-mismatch.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.value: Read-only: does not change the GPU preference.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gpu-preference-mismatch.diagnose.RiskLimitations

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.Name
data.value: Test disabling fullscreen optimizations

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.Description
data.value: Toggles the "Disable fullscreen optimizations" compatibility flag for FiveM and GTA V as an opt-in compatibility test. Never part of automatic profiles beyond Aggressive.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the existing compatibility flags for the FiveM and GTA V executables.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that only the fullscreen flag was toggled while preserving any other compatibility flags already present.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the exact previous value is restored during rollback.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.fullscreen-optimizations.toggle.RiskLimitations
data.value: This mechanism is based on an observed convention of the AppCompatFlags\Layers key, not official Microsoft documentation; compare the result yourself and revert it if you notice no improvement.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.Name
data.value: Test Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.Description
data.value: Toggles HAGS between enabled and Windows' default as an opt-in compatibility test. Never part of automatic profiles beyond Aggressive.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the current HwSchMode value from the video-driver registry settings.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Confirms that the value was toggled; Windows must be restarted for the change to take effect.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: the previous value is restored during rollback (a restart is also required for the restoration to take effect).

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hags.toggle.RiskLimitations
data.value: The result varies by GPU and driver combination; Microsoft does not guarantee an FPS improvement with HAGS enabled or disabled.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.Name
data.value: Guide G-SYNC/FreeSync/VRR setup

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.Description
data.value: Guides checking and enabling G-SYNC (NVIDIA) or FreeSync (AMD) through the official vendor panel or the monitor itself, and suggests an FPS limit compatible with the variable range, without changing anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the maximum refresh rate detected at the current resolution and the GPU manufacturer.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not enable or disable G-SYNC, FreeSync, or VRR.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.gsync.guide.RiskLimitations
data.value: There is no public API to confirm or enable G-SYNC, FreeSync, or VRR; the guidance is best-effort, never a guaranteed fact.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.Name
data.value: Guide clean video driver reinstall

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.Description
data.value: Shows the official clean-reinstall steps for the video driver (DDU + official installer) when corruption is suspected. Never downloads, installs, or removes anything by itself. Never part of automatic profiles.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.DetectionSummary
data.value: Does not automatically detect corruption; the user starts it manually.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not download, install, or remove any driver.

data.name: Actions.windows.system.driver-reinstall.guide.RiskLimitations
data.value: This is guidance, not an automatic repair; reinstalling the wrong driver or interrupting the installation can leave the computer without video output, so follow the steps carefully.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.Name
data.value: Diagnose hybrid/gaming laptop

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.Description
data.value: Checks whether the laptop is on battery or has Battery Saver active, and detects known manufacturer GPU-switch/performance utilities (Armoury Crate, MSI Center, Lenovo Vantage, etc.), without changing anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the power state (AC or battery, Battery Saver) and the list of installed manufacturer utilities.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change power or GPU settings and does not install or remove anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.hybrid-laptop.diagnose.RiskLimitations
data.value: Does not control a MUX switch or BIOS through undocumented generic methods; detecting an installed manufacturer utility does not confirm that the laptop has a MUX switch or dedicated GPU.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.Name
data.value: Reduce hardware power saving

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.Description
data.value: Prevents power-saving transitions on internal links. Power use and temperature may increase.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the active scheme's AC and DC ASPM indexes through the native PowerReadACValueIndex and PowerReadDCValueIndex APIs.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Reads AC and DC again and confirms Off (0) after reactivating the scheme.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.UndoSummary
data.value: Fully reversible: restores and confirms the previous AC and DC values separately.

data.name: Actions.windows.power.pcie-aspm.adjust.RiskLimitations
data.value: Not every computer exposes this setting; the action is skipped when absent. It can increase power use and temperature, and no perceptible gain is guaranteed on every computer.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.Name
data.value: Guide mouse polling rate

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.Description
data.value: When the CPU is under heavy load, suggests testing 4000/8000 Hz mice at 1000 Hz instead, without changing anything.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads current CPU usage (the same measurement already used by the existing resource diagnostics).

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.ConfirmationSummary
data.value: Always completes with an informational message; it never fails on its own.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.UndoSummary
data.value: Read-only: does not change any mouse or system setting.

data.name: Actions.windows.gaming.mouse-polling-rate.guide.RiskLimitations
data.value: Does not read the mouse's actual polling rate (there is no documented public API for that) or correlate stutter with mouse movement in real time; the guidance is always conditional on the CPU load observed during the diagnosis.

data.name: Actions.windows.appearance.menu-show-delay.reduce.Name

data.value: Makes cascading menus quicker without changing an already faster choice.

data.name: Actions.windows.appearance.menu-show-delay.reduce.RiskLimitations

data.name: Actions.windows.input.mouse-acceleration.disable.Name

data.value: Disables Windows pointer acceleration without changing the speed selected by the user.

data.name: Actions.windows.input.mouse-acceleration.disable.DetectionSummary
data.value: Reads the acceleration thresholds and level through the Windows SystemParametersInfo API.

data.name: Actions.windows.input.mouse-acceleration.disable.RiskLimitations

data.name: Actions.windows.storage.trim-status.diagnose.RiskLimitations
